Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with 3-day history of acute watery diarrhea (5–6×/day) after brief episode of vomiting; clinician impression of viral gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery, loose stools x3 days, 5–6 times/day.  
• Associated symptoms: Initial nausea/vomiting (resolved); feels dehydrated; poor appetite; generalized weakness; transient low-grade fever early on.  
• Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool; no abdominal pain; no headache or myalgia; no recent sick contacts or suspicious food intake.  
• Past medical history: Asthma.  
• Medications: Salbutamol (blue) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father – hypertension, deceased from bowel cancer; Mother – type 2 diabetes.  
• Social: Lives alone; software engineer; nonsmoker; infrequent social alcohol use.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Physical exam: Not documented.

Impression:
• Likely acute viral gastroenteritis causing dehydration.

Plan:
• Encourage generous oral hydration; recommend oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
• Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol as needed for fever/weakness.  
• Rest and remain off work; may resume after 24–48 h diarrhea-free.  
• Follow-up: If symptoms persist beyond 5–7 days or worsen, return for reassessment.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Objective vitals, abdominal exam, medication dose/frequency, immunization status.  
● No internal transcript conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality good; minor filler words but clinically clear.
